target_customer: Software developers and QA teams, with paid team and enterprise plans
problem: Developers wait on backend teams or flaky staging environments; testing front end changes against production data or mocked APIs requires redeploys.
business_model: Open source core with paid team and enterprise subscriptions (freemium SaaS)
product_category: Developer tools: HTTP interception, API mocking and API client

founders.name: Sachin Jain
founders.background_notes: Built the original Chrome extension to test JavaScript changes on live sites, then left his job to work on it full time.

founders.name: Sagar Soni
education: Master's degree (in progress when he joined)
founders.background_notes: Joined to turn the extension into a broader debugging platform.

exit.reason: BrowserStack announced the acquisition on 6 May 2025 for an undisclosed sum; Requestly stays open source and operates independently.

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser extension intercepting requests is modest engineering; the later desktop client and collaboration features added scope but remained standard.

defensibility.rationale: Open source code and a crowded API tooling space meant easy copying; user installs and team workspaces give limited lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established tools stayed dominant; BrowserStack, a testing platform, bought Requestly in May 2025.

market_need_then: Developers relied on tools like Postman, proxies and header modifiers, and the founder's extension spread among developers on its own; the company cites 200,000 installs used at large enterprises.

identity.voice_and_tone: confident, concise, punchy lines such as No bloat, no lag, no noise

branding.community_and_virality: Spread through developer word of mouth as a Chrome extension with 200,000+ installs; open source repository and a podcast interview about building it accidentally.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized among web developers and listed on alternatives sites, and the brand is kept after acquisition, but mainly known as a niche utility.

pivots.from: Chrome extension for redirecting and modifying requests
pivots.to: Broader API client and mocking platform positioned against Postman
pivots.why: Founders and CTO aimed to build a broader debugging platform; later an API client was added.

outcome_analysis: Requestly grew bottom up from a developer's Chrome extension to 200,000 plus installs, backed by YC and Sequoia Surge, and was acquired by BrowserStack in May 2025 after adding an API client. Public funding amounts are unknown, but the product led spread and small footprint suggest a capital efficient path to a strategic exit.
notes: Funding: BrowserStack says Requestly was funded by Y Combinator, PeakXV (Sequoia Surge) and angels, but no amount or date was stated. Aggregators give a 125K seed in March 2022 and 500K total; single aggregator figures, so unverified and not recorded as rounds. Competitor names (Postman, Insomnia, Charles Proxy, Fiddler, ModHeader) come only from the company's undated or current marketing pages, so the dated list is empty. Founding year conflicts: BrowserStack says it began in 2018, directories say 2019 or 2021. The pivot date is approximate. Product Hunt and podcast sources were not fetched.
